questions.question: What is the purpose of CSM Guided Setup?

options.text: To provide interactive tutorials for end users
To guide administrators through the configuration of CSM features in a structured sequence
To automatically configure CSM based on industry templates
To generate customer service reports

explanation.correct: CSM Guided Setup provides administrators with a structured sequence of configuration tasks organized by category. Each task includes descriptions and links to the configuration pages in the instance where settings are completed.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Guided Setup is for administrators, not end-user tutorials
Guided Setup guides configuration but doesn't automatically configure
Reporting is handled through Performance Analytics and reports, not Guided Setup

questions.question: What role is required to configure case routing and assignment in CSM?

options.text: sn_customerservice_agent
itil
admin
sn_customerservice_user

explanation.correct: The admin role is required to configure case routing and assignment features in CSM. This includes creating matching rules and assignment rules for case distribution.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The agent role allows working cases but not configuring routing rules
The itil role is for ITSM, not CSM configuration
The user role is for basic CSM access, not configuration

questions.question: What are matching rules used for in CSM case routing?

options.text: To match customers with their previous cases
To identify case attributes and the agent resources best suited to handle those cases
To match duplicate cases for consolidation
To match case descriptions with knowledge articles

explanation.correct: Matching rules are based on two defined sets of conditions: one that identifies specific case attributes and another that identifies the agent resources best suited to handle cases with those attributes. Assignment rules are then created for matching rules.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Customer case history lookup is separate from routing matching rules
Duplicate detection is a different feature from routing matching rules
Knowledge matching is part of knowledge management, not case routing

source.excerpt: Matching rules are based on two defined sets of conditions: one that identifies specific case attributes and another that identifies the agent resources best suited to handle cases with these attributes.

questions.question: What is Advanced Work Assignment (AWA) in CSM?

options.text: A manual assignment process where supervisors assign each case
An intelligent routing system that assigns work based on agent skills and availability
A reporting tool for tracking case assignments
A self-service feature for customers to choose their agent

explanation.correct: Advanced Work Assignment (AWA) provides intelligent routing based on agent skills, availability, and workload. It automates case distribution to ensure cases are handled by the most appropriate agents.

wrongAnswers.explanation: AWA automates assignment rather than requiring manual supervisor intervention
AWA is for routing work, not reporting on assignments
AWA assigns agents to cases, customers don't select agents

questions.question: What is Agent Affinity in the context of Advanced Work Assignment?

options.text: Agent preferences for specific case types
A feature that routes returning customers to agents who previously helped them
Agent satisfaction scores with their assignments
The physical location proximity between agents and customers

explanation.correct: Agent Affinity is a feature in Advanced Work Assignment that routes returning customers to agents who have previously assisted them, promoting continuity and better customer experience.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Agent preferences are different from the affinity feature that matches customers to prior agents
Agent satisfaction is not related to the Agent Affinity routing feature
Affinity refers to relationship history, not geographic proximity

questions.question: What do case types define in CSM?

options.text: The priority levels available for cases
Specific categories of customer issues with associated behaviors and required fields
The data types for custom case fields
The types of customers who can create cases

explanation.correct: Case types handle different types of customer issues. When agents create cases, they select the case type that corresponds to the customer issue. Each case type can have different behaviors, fields, and workflows.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Priority levels are a separate configuration from case types
Field data types are part of the data dictionary, not case types
Customer types and case types are separate concepts

source.excerpt: Configure case types to handle different types of customer issues. When creating cases, agents can select the case type that corresponds to the customer issue.

questions.question: What is the relationship between matching rules and assignment rules in CSM?

options.text: They are independent and don't interact with each other
Assignment rules automatically assign tasks when matching rule conditions are met
Matching rules replace the need for assignment rules
Assignment rules must be created before matching rules

explanation.correct: Assignment rules automatically assign tasks to users and groups when the conditions in a matching rule are met. You create assignment rules for a matching rule using the Create assignment rule related link on the Matching Rule form.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Assignment rules and matching rules work together for case routing
Both rules are needed - matching identifies cases, assignment assigns them
Matching rules are created first, then assignment rules are created for them

source.excerpt: Assignment rules automatically assign tasks to users and groups when the conditions in a matching rule are met.

questions.question: Where do you navigate to access CSM Guided Setup in ServiceNow?

options.text: All > System Definition > Guided Setup
All > Customer Service > Administration > Guided Setup
All > Configuration > CSM Setup Wizard
All > Applications > CSM > Setup

explanation.correct: CSM Guided Setup is accessed by navigating to All > Customer Service > Administration > Guided Setup. The Getting Started page allows you to begin the configuration process.

wrongAnswers.explanation: System Definition contains general system configuration, not CSM-specific setup
This is not a valid navigation path in ServiceNow
CSM configuration is under Customer Service > Administration

source.excerpt: Navigate to All > Customer Service > Administration > Guided Setup.

questions.question: Which are valid options for case routing and assignment in CSM? (Choose 2)

options.text: Manual routing using assignment workbench
Automatic routing using matching and assignment rules
Random assignment to any available agent
Customer-selected agent assignment

explanation.correct: CSM supports both manual routing (using assignment workbench where supervisors can assign cases) and automatic routing (using matching rules and assignment rules that automatically route cases based on defined conditions).

wrongAnswers.explanation: Random assignment is not a CSM routing option; routing is based on rules or manual selection
Customers do not select their agent; routing is determined by the system or agents

questions.question: What communication channels does CSM support for customer interactions?

options.text: Only email and phone
Email only
Web, email, chat, telephone, and social media
Chat and web portal only

explanation.correct: CSM supports omnichannel communication including web portals, email, chat (live agent and virtual agent), telephone, and social media. This enables customers to communicate and receive support through their preferred channels.

wrongAnswers.explanation: CSM supports many more channels beyond email and phone
Email is just one of several supported channels
CSM includes email, phone, social media, and more

source.excerpt: your customers can communicate and receive support through the web, email, chat, telephone, and social media.

questions.question: What is the purpose of service definitions in CSM?

options.text: To define the services offered on customer portals
To create connections between products, services, and case types
To define SLA response times
To configure service desk operating hours

explanation.correct: Service definitions create connections between products, services, and case types. Agents use service definitions to create cases of the right type to support service requests for specific products.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Portal services are configured separately from service definitions
SLA definitions are separate from service definitions
Operating hours are configured through schedules, not service definitions

source.excerpt: Configure service definitions that agents can use to create cases of the right type to support those service requests.

questions.question: Which feature helps agents quickly identify and verify customer information during interactions?

options.text: Customer Central
Lookup and Verify
Knowledge Blocks
Case Digest

explanation.correct: Lookup and Verify is a feature that helps agents quickly identify and verify customer information during interactions. It streamlines the process of confirming customer identity before proceeding with case creation.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Customer Central displays customer information but doesn't handle initial verification
Knowledge Blocks are for reusable knowledge content
Case Digest provides case summaries, not customer verification

questions.question: What is the Assignment Workbench used for in CSM?

options.text: To create new case types
To manually assign and manage case distribution to agents
To design customer portals
To configure matching rules

explanation.correct: The Assignment Workbench provides supervisors and team leads with a tool to manually assign and manage case distribution to agents. It allows visibility into case queues and agent workloads for better distribution decisions.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Case types are created in Case Type administration, not the Assignment Workbench
Portal design is done in Service Portal Designer
Matching rules are configured in the Guided Setup or through system administration

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Customer Central component in CSM Workspace?

options.text: To provide a central location for knowledge articles
To display comprehensive customer information and history in a unified view
To manage central routing of cases
To centralize SLA management

explanation.correct: The Customer Central component displays comprehensive customer information and history in a unified view, enabling agents to quickly understand the customer's context, previous interactions, and relationship with the company.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Knowledge articles are in the Knowledge Base, not Customer Central
Routing is handled by matching rules and AWA, not Customer Central
SLA management is separate from Customer Central

questions.question: What happens when a case is created through email interaction in CSM?

options.text: An interaction record is always created first, then linked to the case
Cases created via email bypass the interaction record
Email cases must be manually converted to interactions
Email cannot be used to create cases in CSM

explanation.correct: In CSM, email interactions create an interaction record first, which captures the omnichannel contact. This interaction can then be linked to a case. This maintains the separation between the communication channel (interaction) and the service request (case).

wrongAnswers.explanation: Email communication follows the same interaction-to-case flow
Email interactions are automatically captured, not manually converted
Email is a fully supported channel for case creation

questions.question: What role does Virtual Agent play in CSM?

options.text: It replaces all human agents for case handling
It provides automated self-service through conversational AI before escalating to live agents
It monitors agent performance metrics
It creates case types automatically

explanation.correct: Virtual Agent provides automated self-service through conversational AI. It can handle common requests and questions, and escalate to live agents when needed, reducing agent workload while providing 24/7 customer support.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Virtual Agent complements human agents but doesn't replace them entirely
Performance monitoring is done through Analytics, not Virtual Agent
Case types are configured manually by administrators

questions.question: An organization wants to ensure high-priority cases from VIP customers are always routed to senior agents with specific skills. Which AWA feature should they configure?

options.text: Random assignment
Skills-based routing with capacity management
First-come-first-served queue
Agent preference settings

explanation.correct: Skills-based routing in AWA allows routing cases to agents with specific skills while capacity management ensures agents aren't overloaded. This combination ensures VIP cases reach qualified agents who have availability.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Random assignment would not consider agent skills or customer priority
FCFS queues don't consider skills or customer importance
Agent preferences alone don't ensure proper routing to skilled agents

questions.question: What is the primary difference between Live Agent and Agent Chat in CSM?

options.text: Live Agent is for phone calls, Agent Chat is for messaging
Live Agent connects customers to human agents, while Agent Chat is the interface agents use
Live Agent is deprecated in favor of Agent Chat
They are the same feature with different names

explanation.correct: Live Agent is the customer-facing chat functionality that connects customers to human agents for real-time support. Agent Chat is the interface that agents use to conduct chat conversations with customers.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Both are chat-based, not phone-based features
Both features are current and work together
They serve different purposes in the chat workflow

questions.question: What are Response Templates used for in CSM?

options.text: To define automated email responses to customers
To provide pre-written responses that agents can use during interactions
To template case resolutions for reports
To create response time SLA definitions

explanation.correct: Response Templates provide pre-written responses that agents can quickly insert during customer interactions. This improves consistency and efficiency by allowing agents to use standardized responses for common scenarios.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Automated email responses are different from agent-used templates
Response templates are for live communication, not reporting
SLA definitions are separate from response templates

questions.question: Which features are configured in the Case Management category of CSM Guided Setup? (Choose 2)

options.text: Create matching rules for case routing
Configure customer portals
Create assignment rules for case routing
Set up product models

explanation.correct: The Case Management category in Guided Setup includes tasks for creating matching rules and assignment rules for case routing. These rules work together to automatically route cases to appropriate agents.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Portal configuration is in a different category of Guided Setup
Product models are configured in the Products and Install Base category

source.excerpt: In the Case Management category, view the list of tasks to configure the feature: Create matching rules for case routing, Create assignment rules for case routing

questions.question: What is the purpose of interaction state transitions in CSM?

options.text: To track which agents are online
To define the flow of customer communications from initial contact through resolution
To manage state changes in virtual machines
To configure state-based business rules

explanation.correct: Interaction state transitions define how customer communications flow through the system, from initial contact (New) through various states (Active, Closed, etc.). This tracks the lifecycle of the omnichannel interaction.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Agent presence is tracked separately from interaction states
This refers to CSM interactions, not IT infrastructure
While business rules may use states, state transitions define the interaction flow

questions.question: What does the Customer History Component display in CSM Workspace?

options.text: A log of all system configuration changes
Previous interactions, cases, and activities associated with the customer
A history of product price changes
Agent performance history

explanation.correct: The Customer History Component displays previous interactions, cases, and activities associated with the customer. This gives agents context about the customer's relationship history with the company.

wrongAnswers.explanation: System configuration changes are in the System Log, not Customer History
Pricing history is not part of the Customer History Component
Agent performance is tracked in Analytics, not Customer History

questions.question: A company needs to configure CSM so that when customers contact support for products they own, agents can immediately see those products during the interaction. Which features should be configured?

options.text: Customer Central with Install Base integration
Response Templates with product catalog
Virtual Agent with Knowledge Management
SLA definitions with product filtering

explanation.correct: Customer Central with Install Base integration allows agents to see the customer's owned products (install base items) directly in the workspace during interactions. This provides immediate context about what the customer owns.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Response Templates don't display product ownership information
Virtual Agent is for self-service, not agent-facing product display
SLA definitions don't display product information to agents
